remarks:
Historic Charm, Generous Space & Endless Possibilities in Buffalo’s Lovejoy Neighborhood.

Step into a piece of Buffalo history at 145 North Ogden Street, a spacious home offering over 2,000 square feet of living space, a double lot, and plenty of room to make it your own. Located in the heart of Buffalo’s Lovejoy/Iron Island neighborhood, this unique property has a story to tell. Generations of neighborhood children remember visiting the candy store that was once attached to the home, adding a special piece of local history and character.

The home features 4 bedrooms and 2 full bathrooms, with three bedrooms located on the second floor. An additional loft style area offers in-law or flexible living potential and currently includes a sink and access to a full bathroom.

The first floor offers an eat-in kitchen, along with spacious living and dining areas. The former store space provides an exciting opportunity for the next owner—use it as a home-based business location, office, studio, recreation room, family room, or additional living space. The possibilities are limited only by your imagination.

A convenient 15' x 12' first-floor laundry/mudroom adds functionality and storage, while the full basement provides even more room for storage, hobbies, or future use. A partial attic and abundant storage throughout the home make it easy to accommodate a growing household.

Outside, the property sits on a double lot with a private yard and a detached two car garage, providing valuable outdoor space, parking, and additional storage.

With its generous size, flexible floor plan, double lot, garage, and unique connection to Buffalo neighborhood history, 145 North Ogden Street offers an excellent opportunity for an owner-occupant, investor, or someone looking for a property with room to grow and personalize.

Seller will entertain all offers! Bring your vision and take advantage of this rare opportunity to own a property with both character and potential in Buffalo’s Lovejoy/Iron Island neighborhood.
